name: reference_checker
description:
Use this to check a bibliography, DOIs or paper titles for fake (AI-hallucinated), miscited or retracted references. Input: reference text, DOIs or titles. Output: one row per reference with OK/CHECK/FIX status, matched DOI, mismatches and retraction status.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/reference-checker (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/reference-checker) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.01 per reference checked. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: bibliography
arguments.desc: Bibliography / reference list. Paste a reference list in any common style (APA, MLA, Chicago, Vancouver, IEEE, Harvard). One reference per line, numbered ([1], 1.), or separated by blank lines.

arguments.name: dois
arguments.desc: DOIs. DOIs to check (bare 10.xxxx/..., doi: prefix or https://doi.org/ URLs).

arguments.name: titles
arguments.desc: Paper titles. Article titles to look up when you have no full reference.

arguments.name: minMatchScore
arguments.desc: Minimum match score (0-100). How close a Crossref record must be (title, authors, year) to count as found. Lower finds more but risks false matches. Whole number, 50 to 100; default 80.

arguments.name: checkOpenAccess
arguments.desc: Find open-access links. Look up free legal full-text links via OpenAlex. Default: on.

arguments.name: includeCandidates
arguments.desc: Include candidate matches. Also output the top Crossref candidates and their scores for each reference (useful for auditing). Default: off.

arguments.name: maxReferences
arguments.desc: Max references per run. Safety cap on references checked (each is billed). Whole number, 1 to 20,000 references; default 1,000.

arguments.name: contactEmail
arguments.desc: Contact email for Crossref (optional). Optional. Sent to Crossref as the mailto contact so requests use its faster 'polite' pool. Never shared elsewhere.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.desc: Mode. 'check' = the normal one-off check. 'monitor' = re-check the DOIs (and/or ORCID works) and compare with the previous run's saved state. Choices: check = Check references (one-off); monitor = Monitor DOIs / ORCID for new retractions (schedule it).

arguments.name: orcid
arguments.desc: ORCID iD (monitor mode). Optional. Monitor every DOI on this researcher's public ORCID record (plus Crossref works tagged with it), e.g. 0000-0002-1825-0097. Combined with the DOIs list.

arguments.name: monitorName
arguments.desc: Monitor name (monitor mode). Optional. Name of the key-value store in your account that keeps state between runs (letters, digits, hyphens). Use a different name for each list you monitor. Default: refcheck-monitor-, or refcheck-monitor.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: citation_formatter
description:
Use this to turn DOIs, ISBNs, PMIDs, arXiv IDs, titles or messy references into citations. Input: a reference list or pasted .bib/.ris text. Output: APA 7, MLA 9, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver, BibTeX and RIS per reference, checked against Crossref.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/citation-formatter (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/citation-formatter) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.003 per citation formatted. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: references
arguments.desc: References (one per line). DOIs, DOI links, ISBNs, arXiv IDs, PMIDs ("PMID: 123"), paper titles, or messy reference strings in any style. Each one is looked up and formatted.

arguments.name: text
arguments.desc: Paste a reference list or file contents. Optional. Paste a whole bibliography (numbered, one per line, or blank-line separated), or the contents of a .bib (BibTeX) or .ris file. BibTeX/RIS entries are converted directly without a lookup.

arguments.name: styles
arguments.desc: Citation styles. Styles to output. All six are included in the price, so pick as many as you like.

arguments.name: includeBibtex
arguments.desc: BibTeX export. Add a BibTeX entry per reference and a combined .bib file (LaTeX, Overleaf, JabRef). Default: on.

arguments.name: includeRis
arguments.desc: RIS export. Add an RIS entry per reference and a combined .ris file (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote, Rayyan). Default: on.

arguments.name: sentenceCaseTitles
arguments.desc: Sentence-case article and book titles. APA, Harvard, IEEE and Vancouver use sentence case ("Deep residual learning for image recognition"). Registries often store Title Case, so we convert it; acronyms like CVPR, mRNA and COVID-19 are kept. MLA and Chicago re-capitalise automatically. Check proper n

arguments.name: fixAllCapsTitles
arguments.desc: Fix ALL-CAPS titles. Some registry records store titles in capitals. Convert them to sentence case. Default: on.

arguments.name: listUnresolvedInFiles
arguments.desc: List unresolved references in the bibliography files. Append references we could not find to the end of each bibliography file, marked [UNRESOLVED - check manually], so nothing silently disappears. They are never charged. Default: on.

arguments.name: minMatchScore
arguments.desc: Minimum match score for text lookups (50-100). How closely a search result must match a free-text reference (title, authors, year) to be used. DOIs and ISBNs are exact lookups and are not affected. Whole number, 50 to 100; default 80.

arguments.name: maxReferences
arguments.desc: Max references per run. Safety cap. Only formatted citations are billed. Whole number, 1 to 20,000 references; default 1,000.

arguments.name: contactEmail
arguments.desc: Contact email for Crossref (optional). Optional. Sent to Crossref and NCBI as the contact so requests use their faster 'polite' pools. Never shared elsewhere.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: literature_search
description:
Use this to find real scholarly papers on a topic (Google Scholar scraper alternative, 250M+ OpenAlex works). Input: a query or seed DOIs plus year and citation filters. Output: ranked papers with DOI, citations, free PDF link, retraction flag, citation and BibTeX.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/literature-search (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/literature-search) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.003 per paper found. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Search query. Topic or Boolean query. Use quotes for phrases and AND / OR / NOT in capitals, e.g. "retrieval augmented generation" AND (clinical OR medicine) NOT survey. Leave empty to explore around seed papers only.

arguments.name: searchIn
arguments.desc: Search in. Title and abstract is the most precise (like a database search). Full text also matches papers that only mention your terms in the body. Choices: titleAbstract = Title and abstract (recommended); title = Title only; fullText = Full text (broadest).

arguments.name: seedDois
arguments.desc: Seed papers (DOIs). Optional. Start from papers you already trust. Combine with a query to search inside that network, or use alone. Up to 50 DOIs.

arguments.name: seedMode
arguments.desc: Seed mode. Which papers around the seeds to return. Choices: citing = Papers that cite the seeds (forward); references = Papers the seeds cite (backward); related = Related papers (OpenAlex similarity).

arguments.name: yearFrom
arguments.desc: From year. Earliest publication year (inclusive). Whole number, 1500 to 2100.

arguments.name: yearTo
arguments.desc: To year. Latest publication year (inclusive). Whole number, 1500 to 2100.

arguments.name: openAccessOnly
arguments.desc: Open access only. Only return papers with a free, legal full-text copy. Default: off.

arguments.name: minCitations
arguments.desc: Minimum citations. Only return papers cited at least this many times (OpenAlex counts). Whole number, 0 or more citations; default 0.

arguments.name: types
arguments.desc: Document types. Leave empty for all paper types (peer reviews, errata, retraction notices and abstracts-only records are always left out unless you pick them here).

arguments.name: language
arguments.desc: Language. Optional two-letter language code, e.g. en, de, es.

arguments.name: retractedPapers
arguments.desc: Retracted papers. Flag keeps retracted papers in the results, marked FIX, so you know to avoid them (they are charged as returned papers). Exclude drops them before they are returned (not charged). Choices: flag = Flag them (FIX); exclude = Exclude them.

arguments.name: sortBy
arguments.desc: Sort results by. Order of the dataset. The reading list is always ranked by reading score (relevance plus field-normalised citation impact). Choices: relevance = Relevance; citations = Most cited; newest = Newest first; oldest = Oldest first.

arguments.name: maxResults
arguments.desc: Maximum papers. You pay per returned paper, so this also caps the cost ($0.003 x papers). Whole number, 1 to 2,000 results; default 100.

arguments.name: readingListSize
arguments.desc: Reading list length. How many top papers go into the ranked READING_LIST file. All papers are still in the dataset and exports. Whole number, 5 to 500 papers; default 25.

arguments.name: citationStyle
arguments.desc: Citation style. Style for the citation column and the CITATIONS file. Formatted by citeproc-js with the official CSL style. Choices: apa = APA 7th edition; mla = MLA 9th edition; chicago = Chicago author-date; harvard = Harvard (Cite Them Right); ieee = IEEE; vancouver = Vancouver (NLM).

arguments.name: includeAbstracts
arguments.desc: Include abstracts. Add the abstract where OpenAlex has one (some publishers withhold them). Default: on.

arguments.name: checkUnpaywall
arguments.desc: Find open-access PDFs (Unpaywall). Look up the best legal open-access copy of each paper. Default: on.

arguments.name: contactEmail
arguments.desc: Contact email for API etiquette (optional). Sent to Crossref and Unpaywall as the polite-pool contact. Leave empty to use ours.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: pubmed_evidence_table
description:
Use this to search PubMed and get a screening-ready evidence table. Input: PubMed query strings plus optional date and study-design filters. Output: one row per article with PMID, journal, study design, sample size and retraction status, plus PRISMA counts and Excel.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/pubmed-evidence-table (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/pubmed-evidence-table) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.004 per article found. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: queries
arguments.desc: PubMed search strings. One or more PubMed queries, written exactly as you would in PubMed (field tags like [tiab], [mh], [pt] and AND / OR / NOT work). Records found by more than one query are counted once and reported as duplicates.

arguments.name: dateFrom
arguments.desc: Published from. Optional. 2020, 2020-06 or 2020-06-30 (publication date).

arguments.name: dateTo
arguments.desc: Published to. Optional. 2025, 2025-12 or 2025-12-31.

arguments.name: studyDesigns
arguments.desc: Study designs. Keep only these designs (PubMed publication types / MeSH). Leave empty for all.

arguments.name: excludeAnimalOnly
arguments.desc: Exclude animal-only studies. Removes records indexed with Animals but not Humans. Records not yet indexed are kept. Default: off.

arguments.name: languages
arguments.desc: Languages. Optional, e.g. english, spanish. Leave empty for all.

arguments.name: hasAbstract
arguments.desc: Only records with an abstract. Removes records without an abstract (often letters, editorials and older records). Default: off.

arguments.name: freeFullTextOnly
arguments.desc: Free full text only. Keep only records PubMed links to a free full text. Default: off.

arguments.name: excludePreprints
arguments.desc: Exclude preprints. Removes records with the Preprint publication type. Default: off.

arguments.name: retractedArticles
arguments.desc: Retracted articles. Flag keeps them in the table, marked FIX (charged as returned articles). Exclude removes them before they are returned (not charged) and counts them in PRISMA. Choices: flag = Flag them (FIX); exclude = Exclude them.

arguments.name: sortBy
arguments.desc: Order. Order of the table. PubMed best match or most recent first. Choices: relevance = Best match (PubMed relevance); newest = Most recent.

arguments.name: maxResults
arguments.desc: Maximum articles. You pay per returned article ($0.004 each), so this also caps the cost. Counts for everything not included are still reported. Whole number, 1 to 10,000 results; default 200.

arguments.name: citationStyle
arguments.desc: Citation style. Style for the citation column and the CITATIONS file. Formatted by citeproc-js with the official CSL style. Choices: vancouver = Vancouver (NLM); apa = APA 7th edition; ieee = IEEE; harvard = Harvard (Cite Them Right); chicago = Chicago author-date; mla = MLA 9th edition.

arguments.name: includeAbstracts
arguments.desc: Include abstracts. Include the abstract in the table and import files (recommended for screening). Default: on.

arguments.name: contactEmail
arguments.desc: Contact email for NCBI / Crossref (optional). Sent to NCBI and Crossref as the contact for this tool. Leave empty to use ours.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: grants_finder
description:
Use this to find US federal funding: open and forecasted Grants.gov opportunities plus funded NIH and NSF awards (Grants.gov scraper). Input: keywords plus agency, date and amount filters. Output: one row per grant with agency, dates, amount (USD), eligibility and link.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/grants-finder (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/grants-finder) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.003 per grant found. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: keywords
arguments.desc: Keywords. What the funding is for, e.g. artificial intelligence, rural broadband, opioid prevention. Use quotes for exact phrases ("machine learning"). NIH also understands AND / OR / NOT.

arguments.name: sources
arguments.desc: Sources. Grants.gov = open and upcoming funding opportunities you can apply to. NIH RePORTER and NSF = awards already made (who got funded, how much, by which program).

arguments.name: maxResultsPerSource
arguments.desc: Maximum results per source. You pay per returned result, so this also caps the cost. Up to 1,000 per source. Whole number, 1 to 1,000 results per source; default 50.

arguments.name: agencies
arguments.desc: Agencies. Optional. Grants.gov agency codes or names (HHS-NIH11, NSF, DOE, USDA, ED, Geological Survey; a code prefix like HHS matches all HHS sub-agencies). NIH institutes (NCI, NIAID, NIMH… or NIH for all). NSF directorates (CSE, BIO, GEO, MPS, SBE, EDU, ENG, TIP, or NSF for all). A source is skip

arguments.name: dateFrom
arguments.desc: From date. Optional. 2025, 2025-06 or 2025-06-30. Applies to the Grants.gov posted date, the NIH project start date and the NSF award date.

arguments.name: minAmount
arguments.desc: Minimum amount (USD). Optional. Grants.gov award ceiling, NIH fiscal-year award or NSF estimated total. When set, rows whose source publishes no amount are left out (and counted in the summary). Whole number, 0 or more USD.

arguments.name: maxAmount
arguments.desc: Maximum amount (USD). Optional. Whole number, 0 or more USD.

arguments.name: grantsGovStatuses
arguments.desc: Grants.gov opportunity status. Default: forecasted and posted (still open or coming soon).

arguments.name: grantsGovFundingCategories
arguments.desc: Grants.gov funding categories. Optional Grants.gov category codes, e.g. ST (science and technology), HL (health), ED (education), AG (agriculture), ENV (environment), CD (community development).

arguments.name: nihFiscalYears
arguments.desc: NIH fiscal years. Optional, e.g. 2025, 2026. Each NIH project appears once (its latest matching year).

arguments.name: nihActiveOnly
arguments.desc: NIH: active projects only. Only return NIH projects that are currently active. Default: off.

arguments.name: sortBy
arguments.desc: Sort. Relevance (default) or newest first (by posted / start date). Choices: relevance = Relevance; newest = Newest first.

arguments.name: includeGrantsGovDetails
arguments.desc: Grants.gov details (amount, eligibility, summary). Fetch each opportunity's detail page for award ceiling, eligibility and summary. Turn off for a faster title-and-deadline list. Default: on.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: researcher_expert_finder
description:
Use this to find the academic experts and key opinion leaders on a research topic (Google Scholar author search alternative). Input: a topic plus country, institution and year filters. Output: ranked experts with ORCID, affiliation, h-index and topic papers.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/researcher-expert-finder (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/researcher-expert-finder) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.0025 per expert found. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: topic
arguments.desc: Research topic. What the experts work on, e.g. perovskite solar cells, antimicrobial resistance, large language models in healthcare. Matched against paper titles and abstracts. Use quotes for exact phrases ("machine learning") and AND / OR / NOT for Boolean searches.

arguments.name: maxResults
arguments.desc: Maximum experts. You pay per expert returned, so this also caps the cost. Up to 200 (the ranked pool is the 200 authors with the most matching papers). Whole number, 1 to 200 results; default 25.

arguments.name: countries
arguments.desc: Countries. Optional 2-letter ISO country codes (US, GB, DE, IN, AU…). Keeps experts whose current institution is in one of these countries, and counts only papers with an author in them.

arguments.name: institution
arguments.desc: Institution. Optional. University, hospital, lab or company name (e.g. Stanford University), a ROR ID or an OpenAlex institution ID (I…). Sub-units count too: a university includes its schools and hospitals. The matched institution is shown in the search log.

arguments.name: yearFrom
arguments.desc: Papers from year. Optional. Only count matching papers published in or after this year, e.g. 2020 for people active in the field recently. Whole number, 1900 or more.

arguments.name: yearTo
arguments.desc: Papers to year. Optional. Only count matching papers published up to this year. Whole number, 1900 or more.

arguments.name: activeSince
arguments.desc: Active since (year). Optional. Only keep people who published anything in or after this year (uses OpenAlex yearly counts for the last ~10 years). Whole number, 1900 or more.

arguments.name: minTopicWorks
arguments.desc: Minimum matching papers. Each expert must have at least this many papers on your topic. Whole number, 1 or more papers; default 2.

arguments.name: minWorks
arguments.desc: Minimum total works. Optional. Total works on the person's OpenAlex profile. Whole number, 0 or more works.

arguments.name: minCitations
arguments.desc: Minimum total citations. Optional. Whole number, 0 or more citations.

arguments.name: minHIndex
arguments.desc: Minimum h-index. Optional. Whole number, 0 or more.

arguments.name: sortBy
arguments.desc: Sort. Expert score (default) blends matching papers, their citations and h-index. Or sort by a single number. Choices: expertScore = Expert score; topicWorks = Matching papers; topicCitations = Citations of top matching papers; citations = Total citations; hIndex = h-index.

arguments.name: papersPerExpert
arguments.desc: Recent papers per expert. How many of each expert's newest matching papers to list (title, year, DOI, citations). 0 to skip. Whole number, 0 to 10 papers; default 3.

arguments.name: includeOrcid
arguments.desc: Add ORCID details. For experts with an ORCID iD, add current employment and role, keywords, websites and a short biography from the public ORCID record. Default: on.

arguments.name: maxAuthorsPerPaper
arguments.desc: Ignore papers with more authors than. Large collaboration papers (hundreds of authors) would make everyone on them look like an expert. Papers with more authors than this are not counted. Whole number, 1 or more authors; default 50.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: pdf_table_extractor
description:
Use this to extract every table from PDF files into Excel and CSV (PDF to Excel converter, OCR for scans). Input: PDF URLs or uploads plus optional page ranges. Output: one row per table with pages, header, row and column counts and cell data, plus Excel and CSV files.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/pdf-table-extractor (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/pdf-table-extractor) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.001 per page analysed; $0.003 per table extracted; $0.02 per scanned page ocr. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: pdfUrls
arguments.desc: PDF URLs. Direct links to PDF files. Google Drive and Dropbox share links are converted to direct downloads automatically. Up to 150 MB per file.

arguments.name: pdfStore
arguments.desc: Key-value store with PDFs. Optional. Pick a key-value store in your account that holds PDFs. The Actor gets read access to this store only.

arguments.name: pdfStoreKeys
arguments.desc: Record keys in that store. Optional. Keys of the PDFs to process (e.g. REPORT.pdf). Leave empty to process every PDF record in the store (up to 50).

arguments.name: pages
arguments.desc: Pages. Optional. Only these pages, e.g. 1-5, 8, 12-end. Leave empty for all pages (up to the page limit below).

arguments.name: maxPagesPerPdf
arguments.desc: Maximum pages per PDF. Caps cost and run time on very long documents. You pay per page analysed. Whole number, 1 to 2,000 pages; default 100.

arguments.name: detection
arguments.desc: Table detection. Auto tries ruled-grid detection first and switches to whitespace (column alignment) detection when that recovers more of the table. Pick one mode if you know your PDF's style. Choices: auto = Auto (recommended); lattice = Ruled tables only (cell borders); stream = Whitespace tables

arguments.name: headerDetection
arguments.desc: Header row. Auto finds header rows above the first data row (multi-line headers are joined). First row = always use row 1. None = generic Column 1, Column 2… names. Choices: auto = Auto-detect; firstRow = Always the first row; none = No header.

arguments.name: mergeWrappedRows
arguments.desc: Merge wrapped rows. Join labels that wrap onto a second line back into one row, so numbers stay on the right line. Default: on.

arguments.name: mergeAcrossPages
arguments.desc: Join tables that continue on the next page. When a table carries on over a page break with the same columns, output it as one table with a page range. Default: on.

arguments.name: numbersAsNumbers
arguments.desc: Numbers as numbers in Excel. Write 1,234 / (56) / 4.2% as real Excel numbers (parentheses = negative) so you can sum and chart them. CSV and dataset keep the text exactly as printed. Default: on.

arguments.name: ocrScannedPages
arguments.desc: OCR scanned pages (beta). Pages with no text layer (scans, photos) are always detected. Off (default): they are skipped, listed in SUMMARY and on the Index sheet, and cost nothing. On: they are read with Tesseract OCR (English) and their tables are marked 'verify'. OCR is slow (about a minute per pa

arguments.name: maxOcrPagesPerPdf
arguments.desc: Maximum OCR pages per PDF. OCR has its own cap because it is slow and priced per page. Extra scanned pages are flagged, not charged. Whole number, 0 to 100 pages; default 10.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
arguments.desc: Optional. Hard spending cap for this call in USD (default from PANDA_MAX_CHARGE_USD, 0.50).

arguments.name: run_timeout_secs
arguments.desc: Optional. Seconds to wait for results (default from PANDA_TIMEOUT_SECS, 120; max 300).

name: npi_provider_lists
description:
Use this to build lists of US healthcare providers from the official NPI Registry (NPI registry scraper). Input: specialties in plain words plus states, cities or ZIP codes. Output: one de-duplicated row per provider with NPI, name, specialty, address and phone, plus Excel.

Runs the Apify Actor pandadad0214/npi-provider-lists (https://apify.com/pandadad0214/npi-provider-lists) on your own Apify account. Price: $0.0015 per provider in list. Runs that find nothing are not charged per result. Spending is capped per call by run_max_charge_usd.

arguments.name: specialties
arguments.desc: Specialties. Plain names work: dentist, orthodontist, family doctor, pediatrician, cardiologist, dermatologist, psychiatrist, chiropractor, physical therapist, nurse practitioner, psychologist, mental health counselor, social worker, pharmacy, home health, hospice, nursing home, urgent care, hospita

arguments.name: states
arguments.desc: States. 2-letter codes, e.g. VT, TX. Big states are split automatically by ZIP code, so you are not stuck at the registry's 1,200-result ceiling. If you also list cities without a state, these states are used for them.

arguments.name: cities
arguments.desc: Cities. Optional. Write "Austin, TX". Saint/St, Fort/Ft and Mount/Mt spellings are searched together. When cities are given, the list is limited to those cities (states only fill in a missing state).

arguments.name: zipCodes
arguments.desc: ZIP codes. Optional. 5-digit ZIPs (05401) or prefixes of 2-4 digits (941 = San Francisco area, 05 = Vermont/New Hampshire). Added to the territory on top of states or cities.

arguments.name: providerType
arguments.desc: Provider type. Individuals (NPI-1: doctors, nurses, therapists) or organizations (NPI-2: practices, clinics, pharmacies, agencies). Choices: all = Both; individual = Individuals only; organization = Organizations only.

arguments.name: lastName
arguments.desc: Last name. Optional, individuals only. A trailing * is a wildcard after at least 2 letters (Sm*).

arguments.name: firstName
arguments.desc: First name. Optional, individuals only. Wildcards as above.

arguments.name: organizationName
arguments.desc: Organization name. Optional, organizations only, e.g. "Kaiser*" or "Walgreen*".

arguments.name: primarySpecialtyOnly
arguments.desc: Primary specialty only. On: keep only providers whose primary taxonomy is the specialty you asked for. Off (default): keep anyone who lists it among their taxonomies.

arguments.name: includeSecondaryLocations
arguments.desc: Include providers with an additional practice location in the territory. On (default): a provider whose main office is elsewhere but who also practices in your territory is included, and the in-territory address is shown. Off: primary practice address only.

arguments.name: maxResults
arguments.desc: Maximum providers. You pay per provider in the list, so this also caps the cost. Up to 50,000. With several specialties or areas the limit is shared fairly between them. Whole number, 1 to 50,000 results; default 500.

arguments.name: run_max_items
arguments.desc: Optional. Most results to return from this call (default from PANDA_MAX_ITEMS, 50). Also limits how many results the Actor produces and charges for, unless you set its own max field.

arguments.name: run_max_charge_usd
